question.text: An insider submits a Trading Plan on January 1, 2026. The closing price of the security on December 31, 2025 was Rs. 500. What is the maximum upper price limit the insider can set for a buy trade under the Trading Plan?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the PIT Regulations, the upper price limit for a buy trade in a Trading Plan may be set up to 20% above the closing price of the security on the day prior to the submission of the Trading Plan. 20% of Rs. 500 = Rs. 100, so the maximum upper limit = Rs. 500 + Rs. 100 = Rs. 600. The Trap: Rs. 550 confuses the 20% Trading-Plan band with the 10% circuit band. Rs. 625 over-applies the percentage. Note: Trading under an approved Trading Plan cannot commence earlier than 120 calendar days from the public disclosure of the approved Trading Plan; the 120-day clock runs from public disclosure, not from formulation or submission.
